title: Hosted Inference Connectors 1.0 — telemetry and fallback release notes
author: Priya Raman
body:
Overview

This document summarizes the Hosted Inference Connectors 1.0 release (May 2028). Connectors 1.0 adds a lightweight integration layer for third-party proxies and partner gateways, standardized telemetry fields for consumption attribution, and deterministic fallback behavior when model or region variants are unavailable. The release is targeted at customers using the Hosted API with multi-region routing and partners building managed gateways.

Highlights

- Connector framework: a small, versioned HTTP handshake and configuration contract (v1) for integrating external proxies and managed gateways with Redwood’s request router. Connectors surface capability hints (prefix caching, KV-cache sharing, supported model variants) and receive route assignment metadata.
- Telemetry standardization: new top-level fields for consumption provenance, per-request fidelity token, and connector_id for end-to-end crediting and debugging.
- Fallback determinism: routable fallback policies now support deterministic, audit-logged fallback decisions with optional customer-visible reason codes.
- Backwards compatibility: existing clients continue to work with no change; connectors with older handshake versions will be automatically classified and routed to compatibility fallbacks.

Why this matters

- Customers routing through third-party gateways need consistent cost attribution and observability. The new telemetry fields make it possible to reconcile per-customer token usage across partner boundaries.
- Deterministic fallback behavior reduces flakiness for production integrations and simplifies incident triage: operators can reason about why a request was directed to a cheaper variant or to a different region.
- The connector framework creates a stable integration surface for partners without requiring them to run the full Redwood control plane.

Upgrade and compatibility notes

1) No change required for standard Hosted API users. Connectors are an opt-in integration surface for partners and customers using gateway proxies.
2) Connector operators must implement the v1 handshake and add a connector_id token to requests.
3) The telemetry fields are additive; older clients will continue to receive charged-attribution as before but lack connector-specific provenance.

Connector handshake (summary)

- Endpoint: POST /connector-handshake
- Payload (JSON):

```json
{
  "connector_name": "string",
  "connector_version": "string",
  "supported_models": ["string"],
  "capabilities": {"prefix_cache": true, "kv_cache_sharing": false},
  "contact": "ops@example.com"
}
```

- Response: 200 OK with assigned connector_id and accepted routing policies.

New telemetry fields (required when connector_id is present)

| field | type | description | example |
|---|---|---:|---|
| connector_id | string | Redwood-assigned ID for the connector integration | conn-57b2 |
| provenance_id | string | Deterministic trace for consumption attribution across hops | prov-20280512-01 |
| fidelity_token | string | Short token representing negotiated fidelity/variant at ingestion time | fid-lowlatency-v2 |
| connector_hop | string | Optional short metadata describing gateway behavior (e.g., "prefetch-enabled") | prefetch-enabled |

Rollout plan

- Opt-in pilot (May 12–June 9): enable connectors for 6 internal partners and 3 beta customers. Collect telemetry, validate cost attribution, and exercise fallback audit logs.
- Gradual enablement (June 10–July 7): expose connector sign-up in Console with an onboarding checklist and monitoring dashboards.
- General availability (July 14): full Console support, SDK docs, and public changelog entry.

Operator runbook: validating connector telemetry

1. Query raw request logs by connector_id:

```
# Example CLI (internal) - filter by connector_id and date range
redwood logs query --connector conn-57b2 --from 2028-05-12 --to 2028-05-19
```

2. Reconcile provenance_id across hops: verify provenance_id appears in both gateway and Redwood logs. Missing provenance_id indicates an integration bug that will cause attribution gaps.

3. Check fallback audit stream for unexpected fallthroughs: alert if >0.3% of requests for a connector are falling back to lower-fidelity variants during peak.

Configuration table (recommended defaults)

| config | recommended | impact | notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| allowed_fallbacks | ["same-model-quantized","regional-variant","lower-fidelity"] | Medium | Order matters: first matching policy is used. |
| max-fallback-depth | 2 | Low | Limits chained fallbacks to prevent oscillation. |
| provenance-ttl-days | 30 | High | How long to retain provenance keys for reconciliation. |
| telemetry-sampling-rate | 1.0 | High | Start with 100% for pilot, reduce after reconciliation assured. |

SLO and telemetry targets

- Connector handshake latency: P99 < 50ms (during normal control-plane load).
- Fallback decision logging latency: < 200ms end-to-end from decision to audit log ingestion.
- Attribution reconciliation: > 99.5% of connector requests must have matching provenance_id in Redwood logs during the pilot.

Known issues and mitigations

- Missing provenance_id: some gateways strip custom headers. Mitigation: provide a lightweight JavaScript shim and Nginx snippet to preserve headers; include in onboarding materials.
- Cost double-counting across partners: rare race condition during rolling connector_id assignment. Mitigation: reconcile counts daily and apply corrective credits; fix in routing service (target patch v1.0.2).
- Older SDK incompatibility: very old SDKs may not attach connector metadata. Customers using SDKs earlier than 2026-11 should upgrade or use the transparent proxy shim.

Post-release observability tasks (first 30 days)

1. Maintain 24/7 monitoring on provenance reconciliation.
2. Track connector-specific cost deltas and report weekly to pricing.
3. Run biweekly partner syncs for pilot participants and gather integration feedback.

Appendix A — Example Nginx snippet to preserve provenance header

```nginx
# preserve provenance header through proxy
proxy_set_header X-Redwood-Provenance $http_x_redwood_provenance;
proxy_set_header X-Redwood-Connector $http_x_redwood_connector;
```

Appendix B — Example minimal integration test (curl)

```bash
# handshake
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/connector-handshake \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"connector_name":"acme-gateway","connector_version":"1.0","supported_models":["redwood-chat-v4"],"capabilities":{"prefix_cache":true}}'
```
